title: DeepResearchError
description: Every stdout envelope the deep-research surface emits with `type: "deep_research_error"`. Four disjoint shapes share that discriminator, so `type` alone cannot route: the real routing key is the PAIR (`type`, `error`), and each `oneOf` branch pins `error` with a `const` so exactly one matches. Added in v1.0.3 to close GAP-SCHEMA-OVERLOADED-DISCRIMINATOR-001 — the first attempt published only the `budget_underflow` shape under `deep-research-budget.schema.json`, which made an agent validating a `cancelled` or `timeout` envelope fail every branch of a schema that claimed its discriminator. A schema that claims a discriminator it only partly covers is worse than no schema, because it turns 'I do not know' into a false negative. English-only: these keys are run diagnostics, not search-result fields.

budget_underflow.title: budget underflow refusal (exit 2)
budget_underflow.description: Emitted by the budget gate BEFORE Chrome is required, so it is reachable on a host with no browser at all. Serialized with `payload.to_string()`, which bypasses the wire-key mapper: these keys stay English even under `--wire-keys pt`.

gated_seconds.description: Wall estimate plus `margin_percent`. The number the gate compares against.

shell_timeout_hint.description: Value for the OUTER shell `timeout`, above the CLI budget so the wrapper never fires first.

chrome_n.description: Chrome-like processes alive when the estimate was taken. Host state, so it varies run to run.

next_action_suggestion.description: Concrete remediation, so an agent can act without re-reading the docs.

cancelled.title: signal cancel envelope (exit 130 or 143)
cancelled.description: Written by the SIGNAL HANDLER when a deep-research run is registered in flight and the process is force-exiting. Distinct from a cooperative cancel, which returns the ordinary success envelope with a signal-aware exit code — that path emits no `deep_research_error` at all.

signal.description: Human-readable signal label; the machine-readable form is `exit`.

exit.description: 130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM. Echoed so a consumer reading a file written by `-o` still learns the exit.

partial.description: Always false: the signal path force-exits before any harvest is possible.

timeout.title: global timeout envelope (exit 4)
timeout.description: Emitted when `--global-timeout` fires. A bounded grace window may harvest partial rows first; when it does, `partial` flips to true and the counters plus `partial_results` appear. Emitted through the wire-key mapper, so `--wire-keys pt` renames the shared keys — this schema describes the English wire, which is the v1.0.3 default (ADR-0027).

seconds.description: The global timeout that was exceeded, in seconds.

partial.description: Whether the grace window harvested any rows before the envelope was written.

chrome_n.description: Host chrome-like process count at timeout, always present, for root-cause analysis.

partial_results.description: Harvested rows, capped at 15 results and 15 news items. NOT a `$ref` to `deep-research-output.schema.json` on purpose: the payload is truncated, and under `--fields` it is projected, so required keys of the full output contract may legitimately be absent. Pinning it to that schema would reject a valid envelope — the same defect this file exists to fix.

partial_truncated.description: True when the harvest exceeded the 15-row cap and rows were dropped.

dual_used.description: News rows were present, so both verticals really ran.

chrome_contention_advisory.description: The run detected enough competing Chrome processes to advise raising the budget.

sub_queries_incomplete.title: --require-all-sub-queries refusal (exit 2)
sub_queries_incomplete.description: Emitted when `--require-all-sub-queries` is set and at least one sub-query failed. The run itself may have produced rows; the flag asks for all-or-nothing, so the error envelope replaces the body.

partial.description: Always true: rows may exist, they are simply not emitted under this flag.
